operator_io_quirks: All identifiers are double-quoted in DDL; table/column names are mixed case (Shop_ID, Num_of_shaff_in_charge) — case-insensitive lookup + original-spelling quoting required.
happy_hour has a 3-column composite PK (HH_ID, Shop_ID, Month) and an FK on Shop_ID to shop; happy_hour_member has a 2-column composite PK (HH_ID, Member_ID) and an FK on Member_ID to member.
happy_hour.HH_ID and happy_hour_member.HH_ID are NOT FKs to each other (no parent), so TS will generate them independently — cross-table HH_ID joins will mostly miss.
happy_hour.Shop_ID is both a PK member and an FK to shop.Shop_ID; TS draws it from the parent's final values, then PK-dedup may drop rows.
happy_hour_member.Member_ID is both a PK member and an FK to member.Member_ID; same PK/FK overlap.
shop.Num_of_staff and shop.Open_Year are declared TEXT but store integer-looking strings ('13','2010'); TS String fuzzer will emit non-numeric strings, breaking numeric comparisons.
member.Time_of_purchase is INT but semantically an hour-of-day (18,41,20,27,44) — values >23 exist, so 'hour' predicates are already loose.
member.Membership_card is TEXT with only 2 distinct values ('Black','White') — TS String fuzzer will produce many other strings, killing equality filters.
happy_hour.Month is TEXT with month names ('May','April','June','July') — TS String fuzzer will not respect month vocabulary.
shop.Score is REAL with 7 distinct values in [30,42]; TS Number(scale=4) will draw from [-10^4,10^4], far outside the observed range.
All tables are tiny (6–10 rows); TS choose_table_sizes will produce 30–2500 rows, so cardinality-based queries (COUNT, DISTINCT) will diverge.
No NOT NULL, no CHECK, no UNIQUE indexes beyond PKs; no views/triggers; no dangling FKs; no self-references.
operator_ts_expectations: shop.Shop_ID, member.Member_ID, happy_hour.HH_ID, happy_hour_member.HH_ID: Number fuzzer, int scale=0, range [-1,1] plus ±1/±2 perturbation — will collide heavily and produce small ints, unlike the 1..10 originals.

shop.Address, member.Name, member.Address, happy_hour.Month, member.Membership_card: String fuzzer over 'a-zA-Z 0-9()' length 0..20 with 50% contamination — will not resemble street names, 'Last, First', city names, month names, or 'Black'/'White'.
shop.Num_of_staff, shop.Open_Year: String fuzzer (declared TEXT) — will emit arbitrary strings, so numeric predicates on these columns will mostly error or return empty.

shop.Score, happy_hour_member.Total_amount: Number(scale=4) — draws in [-10^4,10^4] with ±0.01/±0.02 perturbation; observed ranges [30,42] and [4.9,20.92] are tiny subsets, so range predicates will be over/under-selective.
member.Age, member.Level_of_membership, happy_hour.Num_of_shaff_in_charge: Number int — plausible small ints but not the observed distributions (Age 29..67, Level 2..6, staff 3..15).

FK columns (happy_hour.Shop_ID, happy_hour_member.Member_ID) are drawn from parent's final values with replacement — referential integrity preserved, but parent PK dedup shrinks the pool, so child rows may be dropped by composite-PK dedup.
Composite PKs: sample_fresh_primary_keys keeps first occurrence — with small int ranges, many rows dropped, so happy_hour/happy_hour_member end up much smaller than requested size.

Likely FN drivers: String fuzzer on Month/Membership_card/Address/Name destroys equality and LIKE filters; Number fuzzer on Score/Total_amount destroys range filters; TEXT-declared numeric columns (Num_of_staff, Open_Year) break numeric comparisons.

Likely FP drivers: tiny int ranges on PKs and FK columns create accidental ties/duplicates that the original lacks; missing cross-table HH_ID linkage (no FK) means joins on HH_ID accidentally match or miss.
No Date/Time/Bool/Bit fuzzers dispatched here (no such declared types); no crash-fallback columns (all types map to Number or String).
p=0.2 default with 30% chance of p=0 per instance; checked=False everywhere so p is not forced to 0.
